findings.title: traceID and request-scoped fields dropped from 'grafana-data-egress' log event
findings.body: The refactored logRequest no longer emits the traceID field (previously extracted via tracing.TraceIDFromContext and appended explicitly). It now relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) picking up contextual attributes set by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, but nothing in the new chain re-adds traceID, and whether infra/log's FromContext injects the current span's trace ID depends on internals not guaranteed here. Any dashboards, alerts, or log pipelines consuming the 'grafana-data-egress' event's traceID (and, if the contextual attributes are missing, pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname) fields will silently lose them. Either restore the traceID field explicitly or add a test asserting the full log line content.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, hiding log assertions
findings.body: The new TestLogger.FromContext implementation returns NewTestLogger(), a brand-new logger whose Info/Warn/Error calls are recorded on the new instance and never visible to the test holding the original TestLogger. Since LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), any test that wires in a TestLogger and asserts on f.InfoLogs (message, status, duration, etc.) will see zero calls and silently pass trivially. FromContext should return f itself (or record into f) so assertions on the middleware's log output actually work.

findings.title: FromContext fallback silently discards contextual attributes
findings.body: In grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext, when the underlying infra logger's FromContext does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, the code falls back to d.New(), which returns a logger without any of the request-scoped contextual attributes that log.WithContextualAttributes placed in the context. All endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware would be silently dropped from log output in that case. A safer fallback would attempt to re-apply the contextual attributes from the context.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the Logger interface is a breaking change for implementers
findings.body: Adding a new method FromContext(context.Context) Logger to the exported plugins/log.Logger interface breaks compilation for any external package that implements Logger (the PR itself had to patch the in-repo fake in fake.go, confirming this). If pkg/plugins/log is consumed outside the repository or by plugins/tests in other modules, this needs a note or a versioning consideration.

findings.title: Test name and coverage not updated for the rename/refactor
findings.body: The test is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware although the middleware is now MetricsMiddleware, and no test was added for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or for the LoggerMiddleware's new FromContext-based logging. The contextual-logger behavior (endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes appearing in 'Plugin Request Completed' logs) is completely untested, so regressions in attribute propagation would go unnoticed.
